passages.note: House Third Reading roll call showing Carter voting Y on a divided 31-26 passage, so the near-unanimous rule does not apply.

passages.provision_quote: Except for a form produced by the United States election assistance commission, any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Enacted text of the same instrument; the operative clause conditions registration on documentary evidence of citizenship, and the bill's weaker identity clauses (ID number, proof of location of residence) are coded beside it, not instead of it.
Bill overview listing Carter as a co-sponsor of the same instrument, which was signed into law as Chapter 99.

rows.reasoning: Carter co-sponsored HB 2492 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading (Passed 31-26-3-0-0), an act within his 2021-2023 term in this chamber. The enacted text provides that "any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship" and that the recorder "shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship", which matches the rung "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote." clause for clause: a document proving citizenship, demanded at registration.
